newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover surges in week to Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover surges in week to Feb 7.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange said on Monday its turnover rose 61.2 percent in the week ending February 7 over the previous week, due to renewed share trading.
Turnover rose to 54.323 million dinars ($9.917 million) in 149 transations, with shares accounting for four deals worth 25.5 million dinars.
If shares are excluded, the BSE turnover in its traditional financial instruments stood at 28.823 million dinars in 145 deals, down on 33.701 million dinars in 159 deals a week ago.
"This market is seeing less and less money and borrowers are becoming even more indebted. And those few investors are extremely reluctant to do any business," a trader told Reuters.
Traders blamed tough central bank monetary policy for tight liquidity of the banking sector.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) said it would block any credit activity of insolvent commercial banks, seen as a major threat to the country's monetary stability.
Ailing Yugoslav banks had around 60 million dinars of free funds early on Monday.

Traders said the worst has not come yet and expected another decline in the market activity towards February 28, when companies and banks submit annual balance sheets and pay taxes. They expected market activity to pick up by mid-March.
Promises by Serbia's government to pay late wages and a sizeable debt to farmers was seen as another threat to the fragile market.
With 800 million dinars in debt to farmers, Serbia's government came under increasing pressure to repay what it owes or face farmers boycotting spring sowing.

"The government only tries to avoid social tensions. But it's common knowledge there are no funds from what they call 'non-inflationary real sources' and if they do pay all they promised, we'll see the central bank resorting to the printing presses once again," another trader said.
Traders feared such a move would lead to a fresh attack on the dinar, which tumbled over the New Year and Christmas holidays after sizeable payments of late pensions and wages made late in December.
The dinar fell to as low as 4.3 to the German mark, from its 3.8 pre-New Year level, but recouped its losses after NBY stepped in with measures aimed at sopping up surplus liquidity.
For the week ending February 7, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 123 times for a volume of 17.478 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for 17 deals worth 3.12 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 793 percent.
* There were two deals in the central bank short-term bonds worth 3.2 million dinars.
NBY refrained last week from its regular monthly auction, because its two January tranches were not sold, traders said.
* Wheat contracts traded twice for a total of 4.525 million dinars.
*OTC trade in commercial paper and treasury bills stood at 30.159 million dinars, down on 38.238 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money deals, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, fell to 25.630 million from 35.592 million dinars a week ago.
-- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
